scope: Five fixed synthetic diagnostics with 101 successful calls each, real SQLCipher and explicit in-memory fixture keys. No ordinary project, vault, credentials, security settings, product code, or benchmark target changed. These runs are not qualification or evidence of a reviewed performance baseline.

diagnostics.observation: Inclusive wall/thread-CPU attribution. Windows thread-CPU observations were quantized to 15.625 ms; per-call differences do not identify a waiting mechanism. Held-open and commit variance, not growing configuration cost, explained observed slow calls.

Finer held-open attribution: descriptor-open median 3.2242 ms and p95 5.612 ms. Driver-connect median 0.1013 ms; key setup 0.0374 ms. Different access modes mean later metadata/driver opens do not establish that replacing the first open is safe or faster.

Same diagnostic in separately authorized normal host execution: descriptor-open median 3.2821 ms/p95 8.6759 ms; invocation median 21.3292 ms/p95 26.8436 ms. This does not support attributing the overhead to the managed execution context. No protection was disabled or bypassed.

Instrumented cProfile: 1010 task decodes, 303 result decodes and 82416 schema-node visits across 101 calls. Schema validation inclusive time was 517.5958 ms under the profiler, not uninstrumented gateway cost.

Single-thread prototype reused the exact previously decoded task identity in 707 of 1010 decoder calls. Invocation median 20.2837 ms/p95 23.6875 ms is diagnostic only, not a controlled comparative speedup or qualifying PASS. The prototype lacks the complete prospective deep-cacheability and lifetime controls and is not a product implementation.

evidenceLimits: All reported phase percentiles include one cold and 100 warm observations; do not compare them as the qualifying benchmark's warm-only percentiles.
Inclusive phase timings overlap and must not be summed.
Report digests bind retained bytes, not an independent assertion that a producer ran. Tool execution and independent review remain distinct evidence.
Each diagnostic retained its complete raw samples/profile and source hashes locally; before/after equality is not a proof against transient mutation.
Prior adverse qualification remains unchanged: 12 of 13 selected checks passed; the protected gateway benchmark failed its unchanged 25 ms p95 criterion.
No native descriptor replacement, persistent connection cache, deferred durability, or public acceptance relaxation was implemented.

findings: Cross-transaction circuit and history rereads establish fresh authority and cannot be removed as duplicates.

Successful task decoding alone does not prove cacheability: scalar subclasses and string-subclass keys can survive the current owning function. Non-cacheable values must retain full existing validation and acceptance.

A prospective pure-task memo must use exact returned snapshot identity, bounded strong references, deep exact-builtin cacheability, creator-thread checks and shared active-state invalidation at scope exit. No permission, history, result, deadline or principal reuse.
Adding lifecycle state to the completed generic decoder has a supplemental refactoring portion; diagnostic hits do not establish W1 budget capacity.

integration: No local main integration or formal task submission: the known failing/unreviewed T03 ancestry remains on the campaign branch.
